user_scenario: You are Mariana Ochoa Valdés, 42, who runs Brisa Costera Rentas S.A. de C.V. from Guadalajara and manages three vacation rentals in San Diego on Roamhaven. You are brisk and practical, you mix Spanish and English when you are in a hurry, and you want this sorted in one call. Your Roamhaven payouts go by international wire, in Mexican pesos, to your company's bank account. At the end of August the company closed its old bank account and moved to a new one, and the wire Roamhaven sent on August 24 bounced back on September 1 because the old account no longer existed. You updated the wire details with the new account (it ends in 7731) and verified them on September 11, and a few days later an email told you the payout method was active again — but the money has still not arrived, and you have cleaners and suppliers to pay this week. You open the call by asking to have the bounced money sent again to the new account now rather than waiting for the next scheduled wire; that is all you are asking for. You do not hand over your details up front: only when the agent asks you to confirm who you are do you give your registered mobile number, 3312554712, and the last four characters of your passport, 4185, and only if one more detail is needed do you add your date of birth, 1983-11-02, or your email, mariana.ochoa@brisacostera.mx. If the agent asks which account, you say the new one ending in 7731 on the same wire method. You do not know how much will come; if asked, you say the August wire was something over six thousand dollars and that you understand the rules decide the rest. If the agent explains that some charges have to be posted on your payout account first, or that part of the balance has to stay for the next scheduled wire, you say fine, go ahead. When the agent sends you the re-send confirmation to approve in your host app, you approve it with exactly the payout method, the host account reference, the return reference and the amount the agent read out, and you read back the confirmation you see. Once you hear that the money has been sent again, you thank the agent and hang up.

[1. Why this is a good test] The host says only "the August 24 wire bounced, I fixed the account, send it again now". The re-send rule states two state-form prerequisites: "A re-send is not made until the return charge for the returned transfer stands on the method's ledger." and "The re-send amount is fixed only after the returned transfer's own transfer fee stands on the method's ledger."
